Scientists from the British Geological Survey and University College London have created the most detailed map yet of groundwater resources across Africa, revealing that the continent has sufficient hidden water reserves to support low-yielding water supplies for drinking and irrigation, despite being home to over 300 million people without access to safe drinking water.

Lord O'Donnell, a former cabinet secretary, warned that the UK's departure from the EU, or Brexit, will be a "difficult" and "unprecedented challenge" that may take "years and years and years" to complete, and that the probability of the UK not leaving the EU is "very, very low."

A 22-year-old woman, Sian O'Callaghan, has gone missing after leaving a nightclub in Marlborough, England, and a massive search effort is underway, involving over 400 people and 60 police officers, with a £20,000 reward being offered to aid in her safe return.

In the second practice session for the Chinese Grand Prix, Kimi Raikkonen led the times, with his Ferrari teammate Sebastian Vettel hinting that Ferrari could potentially challenge Mercedes for the win, but also noting that it's early to put too much importance on the times.

Northern Ireland's former mayor Kim Fenton, who was born with birth defects due to the use of the Thalidomide drug, is part of a campaign to secure compensation from Germany, which she believes is close to a breakthrough, and is calling on politicians like Arlene Foster to add their voices in support.

Eli Wallach, a versatile character actor known for his wide range of roles in a six-decade career, received an honorary Oscar in 2011 for his contributions to film, despite never being nominated for a competitive Oscar.

Hanson Academy enforced its strict school uniform policy, sending home nearly 10% of pupils on Tuesday for various uniform infractions, sparking complaints from parents who claim they were not adequately informed about the policy changes.

Violence broke out in Beirut, Lebanon, following the shooting death of two anti-Syrian Sunni clerics, with clashes between pro- and anti-Syrian Sunni groups, but largely contained, and prompting calls for restraint from leaders.

Nick Clegg argued that a minority government would be unstable and that the country needs a "stable and strong" coalition, preferably involving his Liberal Democrats, to avoid a second election and prioritize the national interest over party politics.

Liverpool suffered a second-half collapse, losing to Sevilla in the Champions League final and missing out on European football next season, with manager Jurgen Klopp promising to use the defeat as a learning experience and promising to strengthen the team in the summer.
A man, identified as Ikram Elahi, was fatally stabbed in the Sparkbrook area of Birmingham, with two other men injured, one critically, and police arrested five men in connection with the incident.

Seventeen major banks, including Barclays, JP Morgan, and HSBC, are facing a two-year investigation and potential fines in South Africa for allegedly colluding to manipulate currency markets as far back as 2007, with the competition commission calling for a 10% fine on their in-country annual turnover.

Jonathan Bell, a DUP MLA, alleged that two DUP special advisers, Nigel Robinson and Timothy Johnston, had "extensive interests in the poultry industry" and had influenced the Renewable Heat Incentive (RHI) scheme, but both Robinson and Johnston denied the claims.

Scientists have developed a technique called GESTALT, which uses a "molecular tape recorder" to record the history of individual cells in an organism, allowing researchers to track the lineage of trillions of cells and potentially revolutionize our understanding of development, disease, and cancer.

A businessman, identified as WB, has been refused permission to prevent the publication of his details by the Department for the Economy, which plans to release a list of recipients of the Renewable Heat Incentive (RHI) scheme next week, despite WB's claim that it would cause reputational damage and financial losses.

Oscar Pistorius, the South African amputee sprinter, was sentenced to five years in prison for culpable homicide in the shooting death of his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp, with the possibility of serving only 10 months before being released on good behavior.

Tunisia, still reeling from its worst-ever terror attack, is facing a severe threat to its tourism industry, with thousands of holidaymakers already leaving the country and the government scrambling to address a worrying rise in Islamist attacks.

British Foreign Secretary Philip Hammond's visit to Tripoli is intended to provide visible international backing for the fledgling Government of National Accord, with a focus on combating Islamic State, people smuggling, and terrorism, and potentially involving a military dimension.

The Beyond Caravaggio exhibition at the Scottish National Gallery features the work of Italian artist Michelangelo Merisi da Caravaggio and 30 other European artists who were influenced by him, showcasing a range of paintings that highlight Caravaggio's revolutionary approach to art and his impact on the development of early 17th-century art.

Two men, Virgilio Correia and Christopher Menaul, were sentenced to at least 16 and 9 years in prison, respectively, for the murder of Wing Fu Cheung, who was stabbed 18 times during a robbery in 2015, and for wounding his wife and committing robbery.

The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) has announced changes to the county cricket schedule, including a reduced number of games, a new two-division structure, and a more attractive time slot for the T20 Blast, with the aim of making the sport more appealing to future generations.

The US economy posted a 2.6% annualized growth in the fourth quarter, driven by a 4.3% rise in consumer spending, but business investment fell by 1.9%, sparking concerns about the sustainability of the growth and potential delays in interest rate hikes.

The devolution of corporation tax to Northern Ireland, which would allow the region to match the Republic of Ireland's 12.5% rate, is in jeopardy due to the failure of the Welfare Reform Bill to pass, potentially jeopardizing significant employment growth opportunities and increasing inequality.

Chris Rea, a British singer-songwriter, shares his passion for Formula 1, recalling memories of witnessing iconic drivers like Ayrton Senna and Eddie Irvine, and expressing disappointment with the current state of the sport, citing its loss of mechanical appeal and connection with its roots.

Margaret Thatcher, the "Iron Lady," died at the age of 87 in 2013, leaving behind a legacy as a prime minister who transformed Britain through significant changes, including privatization, and was remembered as one of the most important figures in modern British history.

A mental health tribunal has ruled that Ian Brady, a 75-year-old serial killer serving a life sentence for the murders of five children, should remain at Ashworth Hospital, a top-security facility in Merseyside, due to his chronic mental illness and the need for continued treatment.

Liberia's Football Association boss Musa Bility is threatening to take Fifa's Ad-Hoc Electoral Committee to the Court of Arbitration for Sport if committee head Domenico Scala does not withdraw from his position due to a perceived conflict of interest, given Scala's shared nationality with one of the presidential candidates, Gianni Infantino.

Brock Turner, a 21-year-old former Stanford University swimming champion, was sentenced to three years of supervised probation and registered as a sex offender after being convicted of assaulting an unconscious woman outside a fraternity house, with critics widely condemning the leniency of the sentence.

Stephen Beadman, 29, has admitted raping and murdering 15-year-old Kayleigh Haywood, and Luke Harlow, 27, is on trial with Beadman for allegedly holding Kayleigh against her will, while Harlow has previously pleaded guilty to grooming and having sex with a child.

The UK's decision to leave the EU, as reflected in the referendum results, has highlighted a significant disconnect between the country's metropolitan elite and its working-class populations, with many voters in areas such as the north of England and Scotland feeling that they were voting against the establishment rather than the EU itself.

Thousands of railway workers, including signallers, maintenance staff, and station workers, are set to strike for 24 hours on Monday, potentially causing widespread cancellations and disruptions to services operated by Scotrail, Gatwick and Heathrow Express, Southeastern, Virgin West Coast, and other UK rail companies.

The Rugby Football Union (RFU) plans to condense the Six Nations tournament from seven weeks to six, sparking concerns from players and officials about the potential impact on player safety and the integrity of the game.

Johann Lamont, the Scottish Labour leader, has resigned, accusing the UK party leadership of treating Scotland like a "branch office" and criticizing those who undermined her efforts to reform the party in Scotland.

This weekend in European football saw several teams crowned champions, including Club Brugge in Belgium, Benfica in Portugal, Besiktas in Turkey, and Bayern Munich in Germany, while others, such as Stuttgart in Germany and Getafe in Spain, suffered relegation.

The UK Department for Education overspent £1 billion on the rapid expansion of academies between 2010 and 2012, exceeding its budget by 14%, largely due to unforeseen costs associated with converting a large number of schools to academy status.

The UK government's requirement for nursery workers to have at least a grade C in GCSE English and maths is causing a recruitment crisis in the childcare sector, with a 30% drop in students completing the relevant course and industry leaders warning of an impending staffing shortage that could damage the quality of childcare and jeopardize government plans for free childcare.

Donald Trump, during his presidential campaign, expressed a wide range of controversial and often contradictory views on various issues, including national security, immigration, healthcare, climate change, and social justice, among others.

Several successful business leaders and rock music legends share their insights and advice on running and setting up a business, emphasizing the importance of having a clear objective, understanding the DNA of the business, being digitally minded, diversifying, listening to customers, and focusing on what makes the business unique, while also highlighting the need for innovation, constant improvement, and a willingness to take calculated risks.
